title: Many check methods don't work
description:
Hi, 

I tried a few check methods and some of them are working properly for shiny app. I didn't have time to go over the whole list.

What works:
check.required

What failed:
check.gt
check.between

For example, 


```
iv = InputValidator()    

iv.add_rule("param", check.required(""))
iv.add_rule("param", check.gt(0))
iv.enable()
```

check.required works while check.gt fails (no response)

title: Retrigger validation for dynamic UI

description:
Install from github using `pip install git+https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny-validate.git` fails with

title: Export All Available check.py Functions in `check/__init__.py`
description:
Hello shiny_validate Team,

I noticed that only a subset of the available `check.py` functions are currently exported in the `check/__init__.py file`. The exported functions include `basic`, `between`, `compose_rules`, `email`, `in_set`, `optional`, `required`, and `url`.

However, there are many other potentially useful functions present in the `check.py` file, such as `regex`, `integer`, `compare`, `gt`, `gte`, `equal`, `not_equal`, and many others.

Is this the intended behavior? If not, could we consider systematically exporting these additional functions in the `check/__init__.py` file to make them more accessible?

Thank you in advance for your attention to this matter.

Best regards

mhanf

title: Allow `.add_rule()` to overwrite existing rules
description:
It might be worth adding an argument to `InputValidator.add_rule()` that would allow users to overwrite existing rules. After #14, rules are composed.

In fact, another option would be to give `.add_rule()` a `method` argument, which could be one of `"append"` (default, current), `"prepend"` or `"replace"`.

title: Are rules supposed to be composable by default?
description: In the provided examples, rules appear to be composable when defined in sequence by default: https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny-validate/blob/757c7cdf65191944dce61c89cf71b0b724fa0f20/README.md?plain=1#L48-L49 https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny-validate/blob/757c7cdf65191944dce61c89cf71b0b724fa0f20/shiny_validate/examples/2-deffered/app.py#L26-L27 However, this does not seem to be the case in practice: ```python from shiny import App, ui from shiny_validate import check, InputValidator app_ui = ui.page_auto( ui.input_text("sequential", "Sequential rules"), ui.input_text("composed", "Composed rules"), ) def server(input, output, session): set = ["1", "2", ""] iv = InputValidator() iv.add_rule("sequential", check.required()) # This rule is ignored iv.add_rule("sequential", check.in_set(set)) # This rule is enforced iv.add_rule("composed", check.compose_rules(check.required(), check.in_set(set))) iv.enable() app = App(app_ui, server) ``` [shinylive](https://shinylive.io/py/editor/#) The last rule for for `sequential` takes precedence here.

title: Add py-shiny-validate to shinylive
description:
This may be more appropriate to file in [py-shinylive](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive).

It would be useful if shinylive included this package by default, so that you did not need to add it in `requirements.txt`.

title: Consider adding allow_empty or allow_blank argument to check_email()
description:
Thank you for this great package!

I noticed that `check_email()` currently has an `allow_none` argument, but I'm not sure how useful it is in practice. When using `input.text()` for email inputs, an empty input returns an empty string (`""`), not `None`. This means that even with `allow_none=True`, the validator won't allow blank emails. For example:

```python
from shiny import App, ui, reactive
from shiny_validate import check, InputValidator

app_ui = ui.page_auto(
    ui.h3("Check e-mail"),
    ui.input_text(id="email", label="E-mail"),
    ui.input_action_button("check_email", "Check e-mail"),
)


def server(input, output, session):

    iv = InputValidator()
    iv.add_rule("email", check.email(allow_none=True))
    iv.enable()


app = App(app_ui, server, debug=True)
```

[shinylive link](https://shinylive.io/py/editor/#)

**Suggestion**
Altering or renaming `allow_none` would introduce breaking changes, even though it seems unlikely that users actually rely on this argument for email validation unless they're using `check_email()` for other purposes where `None` values are actually possible. Still, it may be preferable to add a new argument, such as `allow_empty` or `allow_blank`, to handle empty strings specifically. 

Happy to submit a PR.

title: Coroutine 'SessionProxy.send_custom_message' Was Never Awaited
description:
Hello shiny_validate team
I am working on a Shiny Python application that uses sequently the `enable()` and `disable() `methods of an `InputValidator` object. 
When I call the `disable()` method after the `enable()` one, I consistently encounter the following error:

**C:\\...\Python\Python311\Lib\site-packages\shiny_validate\validator.py:115: RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'SessionProxy.send_custom_message' was never awaited self.__session.send_custom_message("validation-jcheng5", results)
RuntimeWarning: Enable tracemalloc to get the object allocation traceback**

Here is a minimal reproducible example where the described error occurs when the disable button is clicked:

```
from shiny import Inputs, Outputs, Session, App, ui, reactive
from shiny_validate import InputValidator, check

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.input_text("email_address", "Email Address"),
    ui.input_action_button("disable", "Disable"),
)

def server(input: Inputs, output: Outputs, session: Session):
    iv = InputValidator()
    iv.add_rule("email_address", check.required())
    iv.add_rule("email_address", check.email())
    
    iv.enable()
    
    @reactive.effect
    @reactive.event(input.disable)
    def _():
        iv.disable()

app = App(app_ui, server)
```

Thank you for your assistance in resolving this issue

title: Incorrect required logic for ints and floats
description: A minimal reprex: ```python from shiny_validate import InputValidator, check from shiny import App, ui app_ui = ui.page_fixed( ui.input_numeric("age", "Age", 1) ) def server(input, output, session): iv = InputValidator() iv.add_rule("age", check.required()) iv.enable() app = App(app_ui, server) ``` I'm guessing it's due to this logic, which was probably ported from R, and doesn't account for the fact that `len()` isn't defined for scalar values https://github.com/gshotwell/py-shiny-validate/blob/de139bfa5bf22705c68f2140a9ed2bc017682029/shiny_validate/validator.py#L205-L216
